descriptionChirho: A divinely granted visual experience or prophetic vision, typically occurring in a trance, dream, or ecstatic state; the predominant NT usage referring to revelatory communication from God. Multilingual evidence: spa 'visión,' hin 'दर्शन' (darshan, a sacred seeing), arb 'رُؤْيَا' (ru'yā, visionary dream), kor '환상' (hwansang, a supernatural apparition), swa 'maono' (visionary perception). All grammatical cases (accusative, dative, nominative, genitive) represent the same core concept of divine visual revelation as in Acts 9:10, 10:3, 16:9.

An external visible appearance or spectacle perceived by the physical eyes, distinguished from an internal prophetic vision; referring to the outward manifestation or scene that one beholds. Multilingual evidence: arb 'مَنْظَرِ' (manzar, an outward view or spectacle, distinct from رُؤْيَا which is a prophetic dream-vision), kor '환상을' (the vision as object), swa 'ono' (a visible thing). Used in Acts 7:31 of Moses beholding the burning bush as a remarkable external sight (θαυμάζω τὸ ὅραμα).
